unit.title: Profile workloads and judge the evidence
unit.summary: Investigate native work, launch, scrolling and memory, then use raw attempts to make careful resource and regression decisions.

lessons.title: Profile one operation from start to saved evidence
lessons.summary: Run a small scratch workload, mark where each phase starts and ends, and keep every outcome when you investigate its cost.
objectives: Identify the scratch target, selected build settings and fixture.
Show which work happens before model delivery and which screen work happens later.
Plan a short trace and keep all accepted attempts, including cancellations.

sections.title: Know what the scratch app runs
sections.html:
A workload is the repeatable job you ask the app to do. Here it is four attempts at the same small job. Android Trace markers only help if the benchmark actually reaches the marked code; the same rule applies here. ProfilingLab is a separate UIKit app with its own Xcode project and scheme. Prepare local fixture creates a synthetic square PNG. Run four attempts submits work to a bounded OperationQueue. Each attempt makes six thousand strings, keeps fifteen hundred distinct rows in their original order, decodes the image, checks a JSON file round-trip, and returns table data.

The fixture identity freezes the duplicate pattern, Unicode title, source image dimensions and output ordering. Linear versus Indexed changes membership lookup. Full versus Thumb changes decoded representation for an eighty-point display at a declared scale of three. Repeat caption versus Cached caption changes repeated UI calculation. These are independent experimental axes: hold the others constant when investigating one. Changing every control creates a demonstration of alternatives but prevents attribution to one mechanism. Preparation deliberately occurs before Work, because producing and encoding a large bitmap is real work.

Only image preparation is excluded; row string construction remains inside Work. This target has no production transport or company dependencies. Its purpose is to exercise a native ownership and rendering path that you can inspect, not to claim that a client workflow has improved.

sections.title: Choose where each timer starts and stops
sections.html:
A metric boundary names two events: start here, stop there. Work begins when an accepted operation enters its action. It ends when the model is ready. Projection, image decoding, file round-trip and UIImage wrapping belong inside it. Queue waiting, main-queue delivery, reloadData, layout, drawing and presentation belong outside it. A shorter Work interval therefore answers a worker question. For accepted-tap latency, add an outer interval in a learner copy and define a readiness interaction. Assigning a model alone does not prove that a person can select the correct row.

Projection, Decode and Disk are nested intervals with separate identities. ModelApplied is an event just before table reload, rather than a frame-presentation metric. ShellConstruction brackets root-window installation in the delegate. It starts after process preparation and closes before UIKit necessarily presents pixels, so it is a launch subphase. Android repository tracing, Activity startup and frame presentation also require separate boundaries, but platform callbacks and instrument attribution differ. Do not turn a conceptual analogy into identical startup semantics.

Separate source-derived definitions, compiler results, host functional results and recorded runtime observations in the evidence ledger. Reading the project proves which action it declares. A completed build proves an artifact was produced for a destination SDK. Neither proves that the destination ran it or that a trace contains the expected intervals.

sections.title: Pair the signpost and check cancellation
sections.html:
A signpost interval puts a named start and matching end in a recording. The excerpt below marks Projection. It belongs inside the companion helper, whose parameters include input and cancelled. Read it with Core/Workload.swift in the Apple target or host compilation. The scratch app selects Swift language mode 5 and iOS 17. OSSignposter is an Apple SDK API available from iOS 15 and macOS 12. Those are separate requirements: choosing a language mode does not make an OS API available, and this scratch configuration does not describe the client.

let state = Workload.poster.beginInterval(
    "Projection", id: Workload.poster.makeSignpostID()
)
defer { Workload.poster.endInterval("Projection", state) }
var output: [String] = []
for (index, value) in input.enumerated() {
    if index % 64 == 0 && cancelled() { throw LabError.cancelled }
    if !output.contains(value) { output.append(value) }
}

The first line starts an interval with a static name. id is an argument label and makeSignpostID creates an identity within this poster. state stores the information needed to pair the end. defer registers an end call on every function exit, including throwing cancellation. The array declaration fixes String as its element type. enumerated produces a tuple containing a position and value. Modulo polls cancellation once per sixty-four elements. contains provides the deliberately simple baseline, and append preserves first occurrence order. The complete helper also polls after the loop, covering empty and short input.

defer does not interrupt a blocking decoder, cancel sibling operations or undo a file write. Cancellation throws rather than returning partial successful rows. A record may retain its cancelled elapsed duration for diagnostics, but the success-latency distribution excludes it while keeping it in attempted-outcome counts.

sections.title: Save one short, identifiable recording
sections.html:
A trace is a saved recording of what ran during a chosen window. Open ProfilingLab.xcodeproj and select its shared scheme. Check the Profile action: it chooses Release, optimization and debug symbols. Signing is disabled in the checked-in target. Physical-device work needs signing in a learner-owned copy. Choose an available destination and Product > Profile. Apple's first workflow uses Blank with os_signposts; add Time Profiler for a CPU question. Keep the actual tool versions and track names. Their availability depends on the installed tools and runtime.

For projection, choose Linear, Thumb, Cached caption and one worker. Prepare the local image before recording the workload. Record one four-attempt batch, wait for pending to reach zero, stop and save the trace. Record revision, configuration, device or simulator identity, OS build, fixture, preparation, pressure state and artifact path. A short controlled recording is easier to attribute than minutes mixing preparation, scrolling and variant changes. Diagnostic capture overhead also differs from a minimally instrumented confirmation batch.

Expand org.example.ProfilingLab and Workload in the signpost track. Select one Work interval and its Projection child before opening the call tree. Separate main-thread execution from the named blocking queue. If Projection is too brief to sample meaningfully, collect another declared batch or version a larger fixture. Extending the timeline into unrelated operations just to obtain a large stack changes the question. Preserve matching binaries and symbols, and explicitly identify unsymbolicated frames as unresolved evidence.

sections.title: Let cancelled attempts finish their bookkeeping
sections.html:
A cancellation request asks work to stop at a safe check. It does not erase the accepted attempt. The controller owns ProfileOperations and a pending count. Each operation captures its inputs and keeps a cancellation flag behind a lock. @unchecked Sendable records a manual safety promise; it supplies no lock itself. requestCancellation sets the flag. The action checks it and still reports its terminal outcome. Operation.cancel can let a queue skip a queued operation's main method. Here that would skip the callback and leave pending stuck.

A host schedule suspends a queue, accepts four operations, requests cooperative cancellation, then drains and checks every terminal callback. No sleep is used to guess when the operation started. In the native app, results dispatch to the main queue with a weak controller capture. Publication checks cancellation again, so a request arriving after worker completion cannot repaint the screen. The worker record can say success while later UI delivery is suppressed because its boundary ended earlier. A screen metric would need its own obsolete-delivery classification.

Kotlin ensureActive similarly needs cooperative checks inside long CPU loops. Java ExecutorService and Future cancellation require an interruption-aware task contract; requesting interruption does not guarantee a blocking library stops. None of these analogies automatically provides UIKit isolation, attempt accounting or stale-result protection. For this finite batch, all accepted operations eventually reach bookkeeping; a production scheduler also needs deadlines, bounds on pending admission, and shutdown behavior.

sections.title: Use the selected stack to pick a change
sections.html:
A stack shows which calls sit beneath other calls at a sampled instant. Select an actual Projection interval before interpreting its samples. Many samples beneath Array.contains and String equality would support repeated membership searching as a hypothesis. Inclusive samples include descendants; self samples describe the function itself. A small self count can coexist with costly descendants. Sampling percentages are not call counts or exact duration per row. Verify symbols, optimization and the selected range first. Long elapsed time with little sampled CPU also leaves a waiting hypothesis open.

Indexed uses Set.insert for membership while appending to the same ordered array; Set iteration never becomes UI order. First verify complete output parity and interruption behavior. Then compare diagnostic stacks and collect controlled confirmation samples with the other axes frozen. Hash storage is an additional memory cost to investigate, not a free improvement. If Decode dominates instead, revise the hypothesis rather than crediting a source-level complexity argument.

The inspected client Performance enum exposes Tracer.shared. That proves an instrumentation entry point exists, not that it emits these signposts, that this workload ran inside the client, or that its exported telemetry shares these denominators. Transfer back to the client as a proposal naming the operation, owner, candidate, correctness obligations and recording plan. Production behavior, device responsiveness and energy remain separate evidence requirements.

quiz.question: Which boundary does Work measure?
options: Tap through presented frame
Worker entry through model preparation
Only membership checks
quiz.explanation: Work includes row construction, projection, decoding, file verification and image wrapping. Queue delay and presentation are outside it; Projection is the narrower interval.

quiz.question: Why use the operation's cooperative request flag for queued cancellation?
options: It makes cancellation synchronous
It preserves action execution and terminal attempt bookkeeping
It guarantees interruption of ImageIO
quiz.explanation: Operation.cancel may skip a queued main method. The flag lets every accepted action report a cancellation. ImageIO still needs before/after checks because the flag cannot interrupt its synchronous call.

quiz.question: What justifies a membership candidate?
options: One whole-trace percentage
Selected stack attribution, ordered-output parity and controlled confirmation
Build success
quiz.explanation: The stack identifies a possible mechanism. Correctness and comparable confirmation are separate requirements; source inspection and compilation cannot establish a runtime benefit.

exercise.brief: Prepare a small projection experiment in the scratch app. Record it if a usable runtime is available, and show exactly what evidence you obtained.
steps: Build Release with a fresh temporary output directory and record the selected settings.
Keep Thumb, Cached caption and one worker fixed; record one Linear batch if the runtime is available.
Select one Work interval and its Projection child. Inspect its thread and self/inclusive samples, then compare Indexed.
Export all raw attempts and leave unknown environment fields visibly unfilled.
acceptance: The record names the target, settings, fixture and exact timing boundary.
The host cancellation check finishes callbacks for all four accepted operations.
Both projections produce the complete expected array in the same order.
Build, host checks, simulator interaction, device trace and production verification have separate statuses.
exercise.solution:
Fix a repeatable setup before starting the timer. Choose the shared ProfilingLab scheme and Release Profile action. Keep image, caption and worker choices fixed. Prepare the synthetic PNG before recording and name worker-entry-to-model-ready as the main metric. The expected ordered result is Row 0 café through Row 1499 café. The host check compares both complete arrays, handles empty input and requests cancellation on a controlled second poll. Its suspended queue checks that four accepted attempts produce four terminal callbacks even after cooperative cancellation is requested.

The trace worksheet records one Work interval and its Projection child, actual thread attribution, and the relevant self/inclusive stack relationship. Until a capture exists, these observation cells remain blank. If selected samples identify membership descendants, the candidate substitutes Set membership while preserving ordered output. If decoding dominates, the projection hypothesis is weakened and the next experiment investigates decoding. No predicted saving becomes a measured result.

The confirmation sheet preserves attempt order, fixture, configuration, worker count, pressure and image state. It retains failures and cancellations beside successful latencies. Native exports begin as native-unannotated because device, OS build, revision and effective configuration still need evidence. A generic simulator build can succeed without a working runtime; record that limitation rather than marking simulator interaction complete. This worked answer supplies a concrete setup and interpretation contract. The learner must supply any saved trace, actual device samples, presentation checks and production review.

repo.label: Client tracer entry point
repo.why: Inspected enum and shared tracer. This is source instrumentation evidence, not a recorded client profile.

checklist: I can identify the actual scratch target and configuration.
I can distinguish worker completion from presented usability.
I can retain cancellations and inspect an attributable interval.

simple.story: A café takes four sandwich orders. The cook puts a timer beside the chopping board. It starts when an order reaches the board and stops when its sandwich is ready. That timer misses the wait in the order queue. It also misses the wait for a server to carry the sandwich to the table. The manager keeps a card for every order, including one that was cancelled. To improve chopping, the manager watches the board during one order instead of timing the whole café.
simple.meaning: Work measures worker entry to model readiness. Projection, Decode and Disk show parts of that work. Queue waiting and screen presentation need their own boundaries.

example.before: Attempts 1–4 are accepted; pending is 4. Attempt 1 has not entered its worker, so its Work interval has not started.
example.change: Attempt 1 enters the worker and prepares a correct model; its terminal callback runs.
example.after: Attempt 1 has a successful worker record and pending becomes 3. That record does not establish that a frame has presented.

picture.caption: The order is queue wait, measured Work, then main delivery and presentation. Only the middle part belongs to the Work duration.

items.label: Accepted
items.text: The attempt can wait before worker entry.

items.label: Work begins
items.text: Row construction, projection, decoding and file work run inside this interval.

items.label: Model ready
items.text: The worker stops its Work timer.

items.label: Screen work
items.text: Main delivery, layout and presentation happen after the worker boundary.

words.meaning: A named event or paired interval marker that a trace can show.
The exact events chosen to start and stop a measurement.
One accepted operation, whether it succeeds, fails or is cancelled.
Stack samples attributed to a function together with calls beneath it.

simple.remember: A timer answers only the question between its chosen start and end.
simple.boundary: The cook is a story about timing, not a thread model. Operations can overlap. Cancellation requests need cooperative checks, and a build or host check supplies no device timing.

lessons.title: Investigate launch, scrolling and image memory separately
lessons.summary: Choose a clear endpoint for launch, preserve row behavior when testing captions, and follow which owners keep images or callbacks alive.
objectives: Explain what ShellConstruction includes and what still happens before a usable screen.
Compare caption and image changes while preserving text, order and display requirements.
Use allocation generations and strong ownership paths to answer different memory questions.

sections.title: State which part of launch you timed
sections.html:
A launch subphase is one part of startup, not the whole wait for a usable screen. ShellConstruction times the delegate's window and root-controller setup. The delegate installs a navigation controller, makes the window visible and then returns. Its interval misses dyld and runtime preparation before the callback. It also ends before presentation and table usability are proven. Android Activity.onCreate has a similar boundary problem through different mechanisms. Start the installed launch recording before process creation; attaching later cannot recover the missing beginning.

Use separate fixtures for a terminated process with an existing prepared file, first-install preparation, and resume with process survival. The app does not prepare its image automatically at launch, so a fast empty shell and a prepared results screen are different endpoints. Record which one matters. A prior launch can leave helpful system caches even after termination; neither force-quit nor a repeated tap proves cold OS storage. Keep exact preparation steps rather than compressing them into an unsupported cold label.

For a launch intervention, measure startup and the first intended interaction after any deferral. Moving image preparation behind a button makes this lab explicit; doing something analogous in a product would require a readiness and error-state contract. The client delegate's startup subspan uses defer, providing an inspected callback boundary. That source is an audit clue, not a captured first-frame measurement.

sections.title: Change caption work while keeping rows identical
sections.html:
A baseline is the version you compare with a proposed change. Both caption modes use the same rows, height, content configuration and image sizing. Repeat caption reverses the secondary text twice in a loop. Cached caption supplies the same string from a stored calculation. The visible result stays identical. This deliberately repeated work gives you a synchronous UI mechanism to inspect. Optimization can change its cost, however. Check Caption stacks in the optimized build before claiming that its hundred and twenty-eight iterations create any particular delay.

Prepare, choose one worker, Indexed and Thumb, then run a batch and wait for completion before scrolling. Fix those controls while comparing caption modes. Use the same table population, scroll start and gesture duration. The native cell creation method brackets Caption only in the repeated branch; record that asymmetry. Caption traces explain baseline work, while scrolling responsiveness needs a common screen-level instrument and equivalent confirmation. A missing candidate Caption span is an intentional absence of that calculation, not a zero-duration frame.

Choose the installed animation/hitch or responsiveness instrument and record the specific track and denominator. Select a missed-deadline interval, then check whether synchronous main-thread caption stacks align with it. A hitch can involve commit work, rendering, compositing or another process. A smaller cell CPU subtree does not establish fewer render-server hitches. Android frame timelines and RecyclerView binding suggest useful questions; UIKit content configuration and Apple deadline tracks require their own attribution.

sections.title: Decode a thumbnail for the declared display
sections.html:
Downsampling means creating a smaller decoded image for a stated display need. This excerpt from Workload.decode uses url, the prepared local PNG URL, and requires the companion Apple-platform Core source. The scratch app targets iOS 17 in Swift mode 5. The shared host helper uses Foundation, ImageIO and CoreGraphics and returns CGImage. UIKit wraps the result in the app. A host check can verify pixel dimensions. It cannot show whether that image looks correct on an iOS screen.

guard let source = CGImageSourceCreateWithURL(
    url as CFURL, [kCGImageSourceShouldCache: false] as CFDictionary
) else { throw LabError.image }
let image = CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex(source, 0, [
    kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailFromImageAlways: true,
    kCGImageSourceCreateThumbnailWithTransform: true,
    kCGImageSourceThumbnailMaxPixelSize: 240,
    kCGImageSourceShouldCacheImmediately: true
] as CFDictionary)
guard let image else { throw LabError.image }

guard unwraps the optional source and exits through a typed error if creation fails. The URL and dictionary casts bridge Swift values to Core Foundation API arguments. ShouldCache false avoids asking the source to retain a full decoded image during source creation. Index zero selects the first image. FromImageAlways requests thumbnail creation rather than relying on an embedded thumbnail. WithTransform applies source orientation handling. MaxPixelSize bounds the longest edge to the requested pixels. ShouldCacheImmediately requests decoding at creation instead of waiting for rendering. The final guard rejects a failed decode rather than displaying a successful empty result.

The generated fixture is square and opaque, so an eighty-point square at scale three can use a 240-pixel longest-edge bound. This does not solve arbitrary aspect-fill crop requirements or color-management quality. A panorama, rotated photograph and wide-gamut source need separate visual acceptance fixtures. A smaller UIKit image frame alone never proves a smaller decode.

sections.title: Distinguish estimated bytes, peaks and surviving images
sections.html:
Decoded storage is different from the compressed bytes in a PNG file. Fix Indexed, Cached caption and one worker, then compare Full with Thumb using the same prepared image and display contract. The source is 2048 by 2048; the host thumbnail check expects 240 by 240. Width times height times four gives an estimate for a common four-byte pixel format. Actual row storage, formats, intermediate buffers and caches can differ. This uniform-color PNG compresses especially well, so its file size says little about decoded memory.

Use Allocations in a separate diagnostic recording. Mark a generation before the batch, run the four attempts, wait until pending reaches zero and mark another generation. Four successful images are retained in the controller's images array, even though the table displays only its first entry. That is deliberate and documented batch ownership, not automatically a leak. Clear displayed payload removes rows, captions and all retained UIImages when no batch is pending. Repeat under the same route and worker policy, inspecting object classes, allocation stacks and surviving population.

Also inspect the transient peak while operations overlap. Four workers may decode concurrently and briefly hold larger buffers than the final displayed state suggests. Releasing all strong owners cannot force allocator pages or framework caches to return immediately to the operating system. Record allocation/footprint evidence separately and avoid treating every high process-memory value as a surviving application object. The host dimensions and cleanup tests establish mechanics, not a safe device memory ceiling.

sections.title: Trace the callback that keeps its own owner alive
sections.html:
A retain cycle is a loop of strong owners. Create callback cycle makes a RetentionProbe with a two-megabyte Data payload. Probe stores a callback that captures self strongly. The controller owns probe strongly and keeps a separate weak witness. Release owner clears the controller's probe reference, but the loop remains: probe owns callback storage, the callback's capture context owns probe, and probe owns the payload. The weak witness lets you observe survival without adding another strong edge. Removing that outside owner therefore does not break this cycle.

After releasing the owner, stop the app through Xcode's supported Memory Graph workflow and locate the probe. Follow incoming strong edges and the closure context, rather than merely searching for a large Data allocation. A stopped graph describes that instant; it is not a temporal peak trace. Resume and use Break callback cycle. The witness calls stop, which clears callback; the remaining cycle collapses when no other owner exists. Then repeat the graph or weak-observer check. The host test proves the intended ARC schedule; a device graph remains a separate learner artifact.

An Objective-C autorelease pool can shorten temporary lifetime but cannot remove this strong cycle or a visible image owner. Kotlin and Java garbage collectors can collect many unreachable cycles, whereas Swift ARC requires breaking strong ownership cycles. The analogy is lifecycle ownership, not matching collection semantics. Debugger temporaries, a retained operation or another callback can introduce additional roots, so a failed release after stop should trigger another path inspection instead of a claim that ARC is broken.

sections.title: Check behavior before accepting a faster result
sections.html:
A correctness check asks whether the changed app still does the required job. Compare complete row order, primary and secondary text, image size and orientation, selection, readability, errors and cancellation before accepting timings. Cached captions must change when their input changes; this fixture keeps its input fixed. Thumbnail mode preserves the declared small square display with a different representation. A phone still needs visual checking. A candidate with the wrong rows or image is incorrect even if its elapsed time is shorter.

Cancellation is checked around decoding and file work because synchronous ImageIO cannot be interrupted merely by setting the request flag. The main publication check prevents obsolete images from entering the visible array. Clearing payload is intentionally disabled while the batch is pending, avoiding a late completion refilling a supposedly released display. Memory, launch and rendering investigations each retain their own failure and readiness denominators. A cancelled decode with a measured elapsed value remains cancelled.

The inspected RMImageCache cached-file branch can create a UIImage on the main thread, or queue file loading and deliver through the main queue. Its later network completion creates another UIImage. These anchors establish actual decoding and callback questions but do not prove the code is slow, downsampled or leaking. Similarly, the real search list uses LazyVStack and row construction; source laziness alone cannot prove smoothness. Transfer a tested intervention only after preserving those production contracts and obtaining matching evidence.

quiz.question: ShellConstruction ends when the delegate returns. What has been proved?
options: All launch and first-frame work finished
One app-owned startup subphase completed
The first result row accepted interaction
quiz.explanation: The span excludes earlier process loading and later presentation. A usability endpoint needs another defined observation.

quiz.question: After four successful attempts, why can four images remain allocated?
options: ARC cannot release CGImage
The images array intentionally retains each successful batch result
The weak witness retains them
quiz.explanation: The controller owns the images array. Clear displayed payload drops those owners; the weak witness belongs to a different probe and contributes no strong ownership.

quiz.question: What breaks the deliberate probe cycle?
options: An autorelease pool around graph inspection
Clearing the stored callback through stop
Reducing the PNG display frame
quiz.explanation: The closure captures its owning probe strongly. Clearing callback removes that edge; autorelease and image sizing do not affect it.

exercise.brief: Keep three separate investigation records: launch endpoints, caption work during scrolling, and Full versus Thumb memory.
steps: Describe terminated-process, first-prepare and resume cases, including prepared files and uncontrolled OS caches.
Keep image, projection and worker choices fixed. Compare caption modes with the same starting rows and gesture.
Mark allocation generations for Full and Thumb, clear the images, and follow the probe cycle before and after stop.
Run available host dimension, corruption and ARC checks. Mark every uncaptured native observation as pending.
acceptance: Delegate completion and ModelApplied are kept separate from a presented, usable frame.
Caption modes keep all row text and UI geometry the same.
Pixel dimensions, byte estimates, temporary peaks and surviving owners occupy separate fields.
The record explains the callback's strong-reference loop and states which break-cycle checks actually ran.
exercise.solution:
Write separate rows for separate launch endpoints. ShellConstruction runs from delegate entry until window installation finishes. Process launch, presented frame and first usable interaction get their own rows. A terminated process with a prepared image is different from first-use image preparation. Keep configuration, installation history and process survival in the record. Force-quit does not prove that OS caches were emptied. Judge a proposed deferral against both the chosen readiness point and the interaction after it, rather than accepting a shorter shell interval alone.

For rendering, use an already populated table, Indexed, Thumb and one worker. Compare repeated captions with cached identical captions while preserving the same gesture and row height. If a saved missed-deadline interval aligns with main-thread Caption work, cache-at-input-boundary is a justified mechanism to test. If the relevant deadline is dominated by rendering or image work, caption CPU evidence is insufficient. The confirmation uses the common responsiveness track; the absent candidate Caption span is not treated as an equivalent frame metric.

For memory, the host proves 2048-square versus 240-square outputs and rejects a corrupt source. Pixel arithmetic remains an estimate. The native ledger marks generations before and after four-image retention, then after Clear displayed payload. A separate probe exercise releases the controller owner, follows the closure's capture back to the probe, and clears callback through stop. Its host weak observer becomes nil after stop. These results distinguish a deliberate image owner from a strong cycle. Native visual parity, transient device footprint, allocation graphs, launch and scrolling measurements remain learner execution; no predicted reduction or memory ceiling is inserted into the report.

repo.why: Inspected synchronous cached-file image creation and queued/main callback paths; no measured decode or retention conclusion follows.

checklist: I can distinguish shell construction, presentation and usability.
I can compare caption work without changing output.
I can follow a strong closure cycle and separate it from batch image ownership.

simple.story: Nora has a large photograph and four small desk frames. She prints four large copies and puts each behind a small opening. The visible pictures fit, but all four large sheets still take space. She instead makes four smaller copies sized for those frames. Before throwing the originals away, she checks that each small copy shows the required detail. Counting the paper kept on the desk and in drawers matters more than measuring just the frame openings.
simple.meaning: A small image view does not guarantee a small decode. Stored images stay alive while strong owners keep them. A callback that captures its owner can form a separate ARC cycle.

example.before: Four successful attempts leave four UIImages in the controller's images array; pending is 0, and the table displays the first image.
example.after: Rows, captions and the four image owners are removed. Framework caches or allocator pages may still keep process memory high; this action does not promise an immediate footprint drop.

picture.caption: These three memory observations answer different questions: decode dimensions, retained image owners, and a callback cycle. They are separate checks, not steps.

items.label: Decoded size
items.text: Full is 2048 × 2048 pixels; the square Thumb fixture is 240 × 240.

items.label: Image owners
items.text: The batch array keeps four images until displayed payload is cleared.

items.label: Callback cycle
items.text: Probe owns its callback, and the callback strongly captures Probe.

words.meaning: Turn encoded image data into a representation ready for image use.
A marked group of allocations used to compare what survives a later boundary.
A reference that keeps an object alive under ARC.
A loop of strong references that keeps its objects alive without an outside owner.

simple.remember: Check image size, temporary peaks and surviving owners separately.
simple.boundary: Paper is only an ownership analogy. Decoded storage depends on format and framework behavior. ARC release does not force caches or allocator pages back to the OS, and a stopped graph is not a peak recording.

lessons.title: Choose how much CPU and file work can run at once
lessons.summary: Bound active work and queued attempts, respond to pressure signals, and compare scheduling with real correctness and resource evidence.
objectives: Separate CPU execution, synchronous file waiting and time spent in the queue.
Explain active-worker and pending-attempt limits, including pressure-based admission.
Plan device energy checks while preserving output, cleanup and cancellation outcomes.

sections.title: Find CPU work and file waiting in the same job
sections.html:
CPU work uses execution time; synchronous file work can also wait for storage. ProfilingLab puts projection, image decoding and file operations on a named OperationQueue. Like Dispatchers.IO on Android, this protects the UI path without making storage free. The app accepts four attempts and offers one or four workers. Work begins at worker entry, after queue waiting. Shorter worker durations can therefore coexist with a longer wait after the tap. Record throughput, batch time, queue delay and responsiveness separately before choosing a policy.

Projection performs membership work and produces stable ordered strings. Decode requests creation-time image decoding. Disk encodes those strings, writes a uniquely named JSON file atomically, reads it synchronously and validates round-trip equality before cleanup. These phases exercise CPU, allocation and local I/O with a visible result. No network or radio work occurs. The fixture's uniform PNG and small JSON are bounded mechanism probes, not representative payloads for every production feature. Version a larger fixture separately when testing a different cost regime.

Select one Work interval and inspect its Projection, Decode and Disk children. Active CPU samples under projection or ImageIO support an executing-work hypothesis. A long Disk interval with few CPU samples can involve waiting, but the absence of samples alone does not identify the storage layer. Add an available file-activity instrument and correlate actual file paths and operations. Do not infer disk latency from a wall-clock duration without considering allocation, encoding and waiting.

sections.title: Bound active operations and accepted attempts separately
sections.html:
An active limit caps operations executing on this queue. maxConcurrentOperationCount does not limit other queues, UIKit, system image services or each operation's memory. This app separately caps accepted work at four and refuses another batch while pending is nonzero. Selecting four workers permits overlap. It guarantees neither four physical cores nor fairness or lower latency. Four result arrays and four decoded images still have their own owners and storage cost. Keep those limits visible rather than treating one queue property as a whole-app resource budget.

Apple documents that reducing a queue's concurrency does not affect operations already executing. That matters when pressure increases mid-batch. This lab reduces admission for later work while allowing required in-flight operations to finish or honor user cancellation. An immediate stop policy would need explicit cooperative request handling and a user-visible outcome. Do not promise that lowering the property revokes executing decoders or that a priority hint reserves CPU capacity.

The queue is a deliberate boundary for synchronous blocking APIs. Swift tasks use cooperative scheduling; async in a function signature does not turn a synchronous Data(contentsOf:) into nonblocking I/O. Creating unbounded detached tasks can move contention while weakening ownership. Kotlin IO dispatchers and Java ExecutorService provide useful scheduling analogies, but their threads, elasticity, interruption and priority contracts differ. Identify the actual executor and its limits rather than treating every off-main mechanism as an interchangeable worker pool.

sections.title: Read the pressure rule as an admission decision
sections.html:
Admission means deciding whether work may start and with what limit. This companion function makes that decision from Pressure, requested workers, Low Power Mode and whether the work is speculative. It is complete when compiled with its Pressure enum and is called before the native controller accepts a batch. Host tests inject pressure values and verify branches. They do not create a hot phone. The app chooses Swift mode 5 and iOS 17; ProcessInfo thermal and power APIs belong to the Apple SDK, not the Swift language.

static func limit(
    requested: Int, pressure: Pressure,
    lowPower: Bool, speculative: Bool
) -> Int {
    if speculative && (lowPower || pressure == .serious || pressure == .critical) {
        return 0
    }
    if pressure == .serious || pressure == .critical || lowPower { return 1 }
    return pressure == .fair ? min(2, requested) : max(1, min(4, requested))
}

static attaches the function to Admission without constructing an instance. External labels make each input's role explicit. The first if declines speculative work under the listed conditions; zero is an admission result, not a valid active queue setting for required work. The next branch preserves one worker for required visible work. The final conditional expression caps fair pressure at two and normal admission between one and four. Equality compares enum cases; logical operators combine signals with different meanings.

The native app calls this with speculative false, so a user's accepted required batch is never silently dropped. Its host checks also exercise speculative true as a separate policy seam. There is no background prefetch producer in the app. Document this boundary instead of claiming that the target already implements a general demand-priority scheduler. A real speculative service would need bounded pending storage, expiry, coalescing and recovery rules.

sections.title: Own pressure observations and record their limits
sections.html:
A thermal state is a system report of nominal, fair, serious or critical pressure. The app treats unknown future cases conservatively as critical. It reads current conditions at admission and receives thermal changes through a NotificationCenter token on the main queue. The controller owns and removes that token at deinitialization. Its callback captures the controller weakly. Policy and UIKit controls change on the main queue. The operation's lock protects cross-thread cancellation separately; notification ownership does not replace that synchronization.

Low Power Mode is a separate signal of an operating power policy, not temperature or battery percentage. This lab reads it when admitting the batch and records that admission snapshot in each attempt. The thermal notification can reduce future queue capacity; a Low Power Mode change during a running batch is not continuously monitored by this minimal implementation. Record such a change externally and invalidate or separately classify the experiment. A production service should observe both signals and retain a policy history so a change-and-recovery sequence cannot disappear from endpoint snapshots.

pressureStart and pressureEnd record worker-entry and worker-exit states. They help identify drift, but cannot prove that no intermediate change occurred. If thermal notifications change admission mid-batch, the initially recorded worker count is a requested batch policy rather than a per-instant active count. Use trace events or an added policy ledger when that distinction matters. Recovery should admit bounded work gradually; flushing every deferred operation at once can recreate pressure. Pressure handling grants no background execution entitlement and is not a guarantee against memory termination.

sections.title: Keep file cleanup and cancellation correct under overlap
sections.html:
A file round-trip writes a value, reads it back and checks that it survived unchanged. roundTrip gives every attempt a unique filename, so concurrent workers do not replace one another's results. JSONEncoder writes the ordered rows and JSONDecoder verifies them. Atomic Data.write replaces this pathname without exposing a partly replaced file, but promises no crash or power-loss durability here. A defer removes the temporary output after reading. The prepared PNG stays for later attempts. Write or decode failure remains an error, rather than an empty successful screen.

Cancellation is checked before writing and after the synchronous round-trip. A request cannot force an in-progress system call to stop, and cleanup still has to run after an accepted write. Projection polls during its loop, and decode has checks around the synchronous call. The callback checks again before UI publication. This staged contract keeps output and attempt accounting correct while exposing the possible cancellation-response delay. Compare cancellation responsiveness separately from success latency when selecting a scheduling policy.

The inspected client URLSessionDispatcher preserves CancellationError and URLError.cancelled before mapping other transport failures. It establishes that cancellation classification matters to the actual client. Its middleware, authentication and request body rules are absent from this scratch target, so do not borrow its transport semantics to claim native file work represents production networking. If a future experiment adds retries, preserve deadlines, bounded attempts and idempotency; faster retries that duplicate a mutation are an incorrect candidate.

sections.title: Measure resource outcomes before recommending a policy
sections.html:
A scheduling comparison changes only how much work overlaps. Keep Indexed, Thumb and Cached caption fixed and compare one worker with four under the same device conditions. Record batch start and finish, each Work duration, actual overlap, UI responsiveness, file operations and temporary image peaks. A shorter batch may require more simultaneous memory or interfere with interaction. That is a product tradeoff to evaluate. A lower worker median alone can miss the queue wait and therefore cannot settle the policy.

Energy depends on CPU duty, wakeups, storage, display, radios and sustained resource conditions. This local workload can expose CPU and disk mechanisms but cannot establish radio savings. Use supported physical-device energy or power tools, retain their versions and actual observation units, and hold workload window, display, charging, connectivity and background conditions constant. A simulator stopwatch and policy branch tests cannot measure phone battery savings. Never publish invented milliwatts or thermal improvement from source inspection.

The decision should name an owner and a recovery action. A user-triggered visible workload may favor bounded responsiveness over maximal throughput. Optional work may be declined at serious pressure. If representative measurements are inconclusive, retain the conservative policy and collect a declared follow-up batch rather than increasing concurrency until a favorable result appears. Rollback restores the queue policy while preserving file and cancellation contracts. Specialist energy analysis remains necessary when supported device tooling or sustained workloads determine the decision.

quiz.question: Lowering maxConcurrentOperationCount from four to one does what?
options: Immediately interrupts all but one running operation
Restricts later admission without revoking already executing operations
Caps CPU use across the whole process
quiz.explanation: Apple documents the current-queue limit and that lowering it does not affect operations already executing. Other queues and resources remain independent.

quiz.question: What does speculative=true with serious pressure return in the policy?
options: Four workers
Zero admission
One successful partial result
quiz.explanation: Optional work is declined. Required visible work uses speculative=false and remains admitted with one worker; zero does not mean a completed user outcome.

quiz.question: What evidence can the host policy test establish?
options: Lower phone energy consumption
Correct branch choices and deterministic cancellation/cleanup behavior
Safe sustained thermal limits for all supported phones
quiz.explanation: Fake conditions and host execution verify mechanics. Energy, sustained pressure and representative responsiveness require supported device observation.

exercise.brief: Compare one-worker and four-worker policies while keeping rows, file ownership and outcome reporting correct.
steps: Fix the other controls and define worker, batch and interaction timing boundaries.
Run available host pressure and queued-cancellation checks; verify separate filenames and cleanup.
Plan matched physical-device batches, then record them only when hardware is available.
Write an admission and recovery decision with separate correctness, memory, latency and energy evidence fields.
acceptance: Active workers and accepted attempts each have an explicit bound.
The record distinguishes initial requested policy, actual overlap and changes in pressure.
Every failed or cancelled attempt stays counted and obsolete results cannot update the screen.
Each energy claim points to supported device evidence; otherwise that field stays pending.
exercise.solution:
Keep four accepted attempts in the ledger and change only their admission policy. In nominal conditions, selected capacity stays between one and four. Fair pressure caps it at two. Serious, critical or Low Power Mode admits required work at one; the separate speculative branch can decline it. The native controller observes thermal changes but reads Low Power Mode only at admission. State that limit in the report. Runs with a later mode change need an external condition history or a fuller observer before they support a stable comparison.

The host proof checks the pressure branches and drains queued cooperative cancellations. Each file round-trip uses a separate pathname and removes its temporary output; both projection variants return the full expected ordered array. This proves correctness under the available host schedules. It does not prove queue overlap, frame deadlines, phone I/O throughput or energy.

The device worksheet fixes projection, decoding and caption behavior and alternates one-worker and four-worker batches under a declared preparation policy. It records actual overlap, batch elapsed time, worker durations, pressure history, interaction and peak allocation separately. A recommendation for more overlap requires a useful batch improvement with preserved responsiveness and safe observed memory. A recommendation for lower admission can cite a measured contention or peak problem. Without those artifacts, the worked decision is a conditional experiment proposal with conservative recovery and named evidence owner. Energy conclusions stay pending; mechanism counts, theoretical storage and a fake thermal input are never relabeled battery savings.

repo.label: Client transport preserves cancellation before error mapping
repo.why: Inspected CancellationError and URLError.cancelled branches. The local file workload does not claim to execute production transport.

checklist: I can identify executing CPU, I/O and queue delay separately.
I can explain active, pending and pressure-policy limits.
I can make a resource decision with explicit unmeasured energy fields.

simple.story: A laundry has four loads waiting and four washing machines. Opening every machine at once may finish sooner, but it also uses more water and space at the same time. On a busy day, the manager lets only one new load start. Loads already inside a machine keep running. A customer can ask to cancel a waiting load, but a cycle already moving must reach a safe stopping point. The manager counts every accepted load and checks the whole batch before promising savings.
simple.meaning: A queue limit controls overlap on that queue. Pressure policy changes later admission, while active synchronous work continues until it finishes or reaches a cancellation check.

example.before: Four attempts are accepted with an active limit of 4. Attempts 1 and 2 are already running; 3 and 4 are waiting.
example.change: A thermal notification reports serious pressure and the controller lowers the queue limit to 1.
example.after: Attempts 1 and 2 are not forcibly stopped. Waiting work starts as executing work falls below the new limit. All four accepted attempts still need terminal bookkeeping.

picture.caption: Lowering concurrency from 4 to 1 changes later starts. It leaves running attempts and the four-attempt ledger intact.

items.label: Before pressure
items.text: Two attempts run and two accepted attempts wait.

items.label: Serious pressure
items.text: The controller lowers future queue capacity to one.

items.label: Active work
items.text: Existing operations finish or honor a cooperative cancellation request.

items.label: Later admission
items.text: Waiting attempts use the reduced capacity when a slot becomes available.

words.meaning: The maximum number of operations this queue allows to execute at once.
Accepted work that has not yet reached its terminal outcome.
A system signal about current heat-related operating conditions.
A separate system power policy, not a temperature or battery-percentage reading.

simple.remember: Limit new work without pretending that already running work has stopped.
simple.boundary: Machines do not model executors or CPU cores. Queue capacity controls only its own operations. Policy tests with invented pressure values cannot measure phone energy, and atomic file replacement does not promise power-loss durability.

lessons.title: Turn raw attempts into a reviewable regression decision
lessons.summary: Keep original attempt records, check their origins and conditions, and read slow results beside failures before making a decision.
objectives: Explain what each raw duration includes and leaves outside its boundary.
Check attempt order and comparable recording conditions before calculating percentiles.
Distinguish bad capture, wrong output, too few samples and data ready for human review.

sections.title: Keep attempts before making a summary
sections.html:
A raw record keeps one attempt's facts before you reduce them to a number. An Android benchmark summary can hide timeouts, preparation or runner differences; an iOS summary can do the same. ProfilingLab retains a RawRecord for every accepted worker attempt, including errors and cancellations. Its ordinal is the admission position. Its place in the exported array is completion append order. Overlapping workers can finish in a different order from acceptance. Preserve both orders and the original file, rather than sorting away the evidence that explains a result.

The worker reads DispatchTime uptime nanoseconds before executing its body and computes elapsed milliseconds at exit. This monotonic duration includes row construction, projection, image decoding, file verification and image wrapping. It excludes queue waiting, main delivery and presentation. Equality against the independent expected ordered array occurs after the elapsed calculation. File round-trip validation remains inside Disk and Work because that verification is part of the defined operation. State this distinction explicitly instead of calling every correctness check outside measurement.

Each record includes variant, fixture, boundary, worker policy, pressure endpoints, Low Power Mode admission snapshot, configuration, revision, device identity, OS build and cache policy. The app exports native-unannotated and blank environment fields because it cannot infer the full recording contract. A learner must annotate a retained copy from actual evidence. Never fill blanks with a plausible phone, borrow another revision's artifact or classify an exported native file as synthetic to make it validate.

sections.title: Read what the JSON export preserves
sections.html:
An export writes the current ledger to a file you can retain. This excerpt comes from the controller's exportRecords method. It needs the app target, records array and root URL; it is not a standalone command-line program. The target chooses Swift mode 5 and iOS 17. JSONEncoder and Data.write belong to Foundation. UIActivityViewController handles the app's user-controlled share step. Sorted JSON keys make objects easier to read, but do not reorder the attempt array or change what each Work duration means.

let encoder = JSONEncoder()
encoder.outputFormatting = [.prettyPrinted, .sortedKeys]
let url = root.appendingPathComponent("raw-records.json")
try encoder.encode(RawEnvelope(schema: 1, records: records))
    .write(to: url, options: .atomic)

The first line constructs a new encoder for this export. The array of formatting options selects readable output and sorted object keys; it does not sort the records array or change attempt order. appendingPathComponent constructs a child URL without manual path concatenation. RawEnvelope labels the schema version and snapshots the records array as a value. encode can throw, and write can throw separately; try propagates either to the surrounding do/catch, which displays an export failure. Atomic replacement concerns the pathname update, not guaranteed durable storage after power loss.

The app only exports after pending reaches zero, reducing the chance of silently omitting outstanding attempts. A weak controller capture in worker delivery still means a destroyed controller cannot append into its old ledger. This scratch app is a single-root teaching target; a production recorder would require durable ownership outside a disappearing screen and a recovery protocol for interrupted exports. Kotlin data classes and serialization offer a familiar immutable-record idea, while Swift arrays, Codable, ARC and UIKit sharing have different lifetime and platform contracts.

sections.title: Check origins and matching conditions first
sections.html:
A validator checks whether records satisfy the declared input rules. Records/make-synthetic.mjs creates a fictional arithmetic dataset in a fresh temporary directory. Records/validate.mjs checks that file. The generator labels source synthetic and leaves device and OS fields blank. Its elapsed values are invented. The validator requires schema one, nonempty records, unique IDs and ordinals, known outcomes, bounded workers, explicit pressure and finite nonnegative durations. Success must assert correct true. Zero is valid arithmetic; a real zero duration still needs a human check of clock resolution.

Observed device, simulator and host records require environment identity, OS build, revision and Debug or Release configuration. native-unannotated is rejected until annotation is complete. Synthetic records cannot name a device or OS build. Preparation failures and endpoint pressure drift violate this lab's predeclared stable-cohort protocol, so the report classifies them invalid while retaining their raw records and counts. A variant mixing multiple revisions is also invalid. These rules diagnose an experiment; they do not authorize deleting inconvenient rows.

The cohort key contains source, device, OS, configuration, fixture, boundary, cache policy, worker count, Low Power Mode snapshot and pressure endpoints. Revision stays within each variant so baseline and candidate revisions can differ while each remains internally consistent. Changing worker count creates a separate cohort. For the scheduling experiment, deliberately design a matching comparison protocol before modifying that rule; otherwise the validator correctly refuses to present the two policies as identical conditions. It is a narrow importer and descriptive validator, not a universal statistical gate.

sections.title: Read percentiles beside attempt counts
sections.html:
A percentile summarizes a position among sorted values. This validator sorts successful durations in a copy. For an even count, median averages the middle two. Nearest-rank p95 uses rank ceil(0.95 times n), then converts that rank to an array index. For twenty successes it selects the nineteenth value. Invented baseline durations eighty through ninety-nine give median 89.5 and p95 98. Invented candidate durations seventy through eighty-nine give median 79.5 and p95 88. These are arithmetic examples, never recorded workload timings.

The report keeps attempts, counts for success/error/cancelled/timeout/incorrect/preparation-failure, successful n, range, median, p95, revision and raw ordinal order. Its failureRate counts error, timeout and incorrect divided by all retained attempts. Cancellation and preparation have separate counts; read those as well because a lower failureRate could otherwise coincide with more cancellations or unusable preparation. A cancelled or timed-out duration never enters successful latency. A candidate cannot improve its tail by silently turning slow operations into cancellations.

At least twenty successes for each of exactly two variants in one cohort is a lab review minimum. It supplies neither a stable population-tail estimate nor uncertainty bounds. More data may be needed according to the effect size, variance and product consequence. Do not average p95 values across devices, or add Projection p95 and Decode p95 to create an end-to-end p95. The slow samples may belong to different attempts. Preserve paired raw phase evidence if that decomposition is necessary.

sections.title: Choose the response that fits the result
sections.html:
A decision class tells you which question to resolve next. invalid_capture means that origin, shape or stable-condition checks failed. Keep the original, repair the harness or annotation, and collect a bounded replacement. correctness_failure means the output was wrong; reject the candidate before comparing speed. insufficient_samples means the accepted records cannot meet this validator's two-variant, single-cohort review rule. Collect the missing matching samples or split the experiment explicitly. These are different failures and need different recovery actions, even when all prevent a performance decision.

review_required means the descriptive dataset satisfies those preliminary rules. It deliberately never says ship or pass. Compare absolute user budgets and paired baseline/candidate change using a threshold declared before collection. Existing MeasurementLab already demonstrates configurable synthetic regression gates; this addition connects raw native capture to those decisions without duplicating its policy. A human review checks failures, cancellations, trace attribution, environment drift, memory and readiness evidence beside the successful percentile.

A regression decision needs an owner, bounded reproduction and recovery. If the candidate violates a meaningful declared budget while a comparable baseline does not, investigate and revert the isolated intervention or contain it behind an appropriate policy. Do not rerun until one lucky batch passes, hide failures or relax the budget after seeing the answer. If both variants move together, examine runner disturbance and changed conditions. A statistically or operationally uncertain result remains pending with a concrete next experiment rather than a fabricated confidence interval.

sections.title: Hand over records, symbols and missing evidence together
sections.html:
An audit packet lets another engineer trace each claim to an artifact. Keep the original JSON, annotated copy, validator report, protocol, commands, tool versions, effective configuration, revision, binary and matching symbols. Include selected trace coordinates and functional results. Coordinates should identify the process and operation, rather than only a screenshot of a large stack. Running a record validator creates no trace. Host image dimensions show decode mechanics; device allocations and image quality require their own observations and remain separate checks.

The inspected client streaming benchmark creates a payload, starts consumption in a Task, waits for an expectation and discards the XCTWaiter return value. That source invites questions about successful completion, timeout and surviving task lifetime. It does not prove the benchmark timed out, nor that its source comment is a production threshold. A result bundle and actual selected runner/test plan are required to establish execution and outcomes. A wrapper that labels every returned measurement successful would conceal exactly the classifications this lab preserves.

The same disciplined handoff applies across Kotlin/Java and Swift: retain attempted outcomes, declaration and evidence, but verify each runtime's timing, cancellation and ownership separately. This course supplies no learner completion, release approval, fleet confidence or production optimization claim. Native interaction, sustained pressure, specialist statistics and organizational budget ownership remain explicit follow-up work when they determine the final decision.

quiz.question: A valid synthetic two-variant report returns review_required. What does that mean?
options: The phone regression gate passed
The lab's descriptive input contract passed; a human decision still needs real evidence
The data can be presented as a device trace
quiz.explanation: Synthetic arithmetic establishes validator behavior. review_required is not a release or device-performance result.

quiz.question: How should a timeout affect summaries?
options: Remove the entire attempt
Retain its outcome and attempted denominator, exclude it from successful latency
Replace its duration with zero
quiz.explanation: A timeout is an attempted failure, not a successful sample. Zero replacement and deletion manufacture favorable latency.

quiz.question: Which percentile statement is valid?
options: p95 of end-to-end always equals the sum of phase p95 values
Nearest-rank p95 of integers 80 through 99 is 98
Average device p95 is always fleet p95
quiz.explanation: There are twenty ordered values; ceil(.95×20)=19 selects 98. Independent phase or device percentiles cannot be combined into those other distributions without raw data and a declared model.

exercise.brief: Validate a raw-record dataset and write a decision that states what the data supports and what still needs product review.
steps: Create the synthetic dataset in a fresh temporary directory and inspect its origin fields.
Verify success count, median, p95, attempted outcomes and admission order.
Make separate copies for timeout, incorrect output, missing duration, mixed revision and pressure drift; retain the original.
Prepare a native annotation and decision packet, marking absent device observations as pending.
acceptance: Synthetic records keep that label and blank device and OS fields.
The fictional baseline summary is 20 successes, median 89.5, p95 98; candidate is 20, 79.5, 88.
Malformed inputs, incorrect output, pressure drift and retained timeouts produce their distinct expected results.
review_required is described as a prompt for review, with no claim of release approval or device measurement.
exercise.solution:
The worked arithmetic case uses a fictional dataset. Generate it and run the validator. Both variants have twenty successes in one synthetic cohort. The report returns review_required and synthetic true, with medians 89.5 and 79.5 and nearest-rank p95 values 98 and 88. These results verify calculation behavior. If you change one attempt to timeout, its duration leaves successful latency but the attempt stays counted. That variant then has twenty attempts, one timeout and nineteen successes, which falls below this lab's review minimum.

Set correct false with outcome incorrect and the report becomes correctness_failure. Remove a success duration, leave source native-unannotated, mix revisions in a variant, fail preparation or change endpoint pressure and the report is invalid_capture. Changing worker count splits cohorts and produces insufficient_samples. The checks script verifies these meaningful distinctions. Restore each mutation from the retained original before testing the next; otherwise compound failures obscure which rule was exercised.

For a real native export, keep the original file and create an annotated copy using the actual destination, OS build, revision and effective configuration. Preserve ordinal admission order and completion append order. The decision record names the exact metric boundary, budget owner, failure and cancellation guardrails, diagnostic attribution and recovery path. The synthetic demonstration cannot authorize release. Until the learner records a matching device cohort and obtains relevant launch, scrolling, allocation or energy evidence, those fields remain pending and the only completed claim is companion correctness and validation behavior.

repo.label: Client streaming benchmark wait and completion boundary
repo.why: Inspected asynchronous consumption, expected completion and discarded XCTWaiter result at line 50. Actual benchmark execution/outcomes remain unverified.

checklist: I can preserve provenance, attempt order and failed outcomes.
I can reproduce the declared percentile arithmetic.
I can separate capture validation, correctness and accountable regression review.

simple.story: A bus inspector writes down every scheduled trip. For each one, the sheet records its number, route, departure and outcome. Two cancelled trips stay on the sheet even though they have no successful journey time. To compare buses, the inspector keeps the route and stopping rules the same. A practice sheet uses made-up times to check the calculator. Those numbers can prove the calculator works, but they cannot show whether any real bus was faster or deserves a new timetable.
simple.meaning: Raw records retain attempts and provenance before summaries. Compare matching cohorts and keep failure denominators. Synthetic arithmetic checks a validator, not real device performance.

example.before: The fictional baseline has 20 successes with durations 80–99. Its median is 89.5 and nearest-rank p95 is 98.
example.change: Change the attempt with duration 99 to timeout while retaining it in the raw array.
example.after: There are still 20 attempts, now 19 successes and 1 timeout. Successful p95 is 98, yet the two-variant review minimum is no longer met.

picture.caption: The synthetic timeout keeps the attempt count at 20 while reducing successful n to 19; a favorable percentile does not restore review eligibility.

items.label: Raw baseline
items.text: All 20 invented attempts begin as successful records.

items.label: Retained timeout
items.text: One record becomes timeout and stays in the original order.

items.label: Decision
items.text: The dataset has too few successes for this lab's comparison minimum.

words.meaning: Recorded facts about where data came from and which setup produced it.
Records grouped by declared matching conditions.
The full count used beneath a fraction, such as failures divided by attempts.
Here, sort successful durations and round 95% of their count upward to choose a rank. With 20 successes, select the 19th value.

simple.remember: Keep the failed attempts when the successful numbers look better.
simple.boundary: Trips are a counting analogy. Twenty successes is only a lab minimum, not statistical confidence. Invented durations cannot establish speed, battery savings, production readiness or release approval.
